Ukraine Strikes Russian Oil Terminal; Russia Buys Gasoline From India

Ukrainian drones attacked oil terminals in Russia's St. Petersburg region on January 21. The strikes targeted facilities in the Leningrad Oblast, with one drone hitting the Novatek gas processing plant. This attack is part of Ukraine's strategy to damage Russia's economy and war capabilities. In a separate development, Russia has begun importing gasoline from India, with reports indicating 60,000 tons were purchased and two tankers dispatched. This comes as Russia's own fuel supply faces pressure following Ukrainian drone attacks on its oil infrastructure.
